deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 6-8): X is a topological space and F_0 is a family of closed subsets of X. F is the Boolean-type algebra of 'constructible' sets generated by F_0, that is, finite unions of sets A∩∁B with A, B in F_0. The goal is an axiomatic, ultimately topology-free description of a 'tame' family of subsets, in the spirit of 'topologie modérée'. The previous page fixes the conditions under which F_0 is exactly the set of closed members of F: (α) F_0 is stable under finite unions; (β) F_0 is stable under finite intersections; (γ) for A, B in F_0, the closure of A∩∁B lies in F_0.

This page:
(1) Intrinsic closure. Assume α, β, γ. For any A in F, write A = ∪(A_i∩∁B_i). Then Ā = ∪ closure(A_i∩∁B_i), which lies in F_0 by α and γ. Since every member of F_0 is closed, Ā is the smallest element of F_0 containing A. So closure on F is determined by the lattice F_0 alone, 'sans utiliser la top. de X'. (A first, struck version stated this only for A∩∁B.)
(2) Intrinsic nowhere-density. For A ⊂ B in F, 'A rare in B' means B−A is dense in B, i.e. B ⊂ closure(B−A). Intrinsically: every element of F_0 containing B−A contains B. Call this 'F_0-rare'.
(3) Restated axiom δ, a finite-dimension or well-foundedness axiom. Every decreasing sequence A_1 ⊃ A_2 ⊃ … in F with each A_{n+1} F_0-rare in A_n is eventually empty. This is the tame-topology substitute for 'dim(frontier) < dim', so that iterated frontiers terminate.
(4) NB, a representation question. Given only a family F_0 ⊂ P(X), when does some topology on X make F_0 satisfy α, β, γ (and possibly δ)? The answer begins here and is completed on the next page. The conditions are α, β, and γ': for A, B in F_0 there is a smallest element of F_0 containing A∩∁B. Sufficiency uses the coarsest such topology, whose closed sets are arbitrary intersections of members of F_0. These are stable under finite unions by distributivity and α. In this topology the closure of A∖B is the intersection of the members of F_0 containing it, which lies in F_0 by γ'. Necessity holds because in any admissible topology the closure of A∖B is in F_0 and is automatically the least member of F_0 containing A∖B.

In lattice terms, γ' says F_0 is a co-Heyting (Brouwerian) sublattice of P(X): the co-implication A∸B = min{C : A ⊂ B∪C} exists and equals the topological closure of A∖B. Axiom δ is then a descending-chain condition on 'dense differences', a Krull-dimension-type finiteness for this co-Heyting algebra.
errors: Line 4 apparently still reads 'contenant A∩∁B' after the correction from A∩∁B to A∈F; logically it should be 'the smallest element of F_0 containing A'. This is a leftover from the struck first version.

'Rare' is used as 'complement dense' (empty interior) rather than 'nowhere dense'. For members of F (finite unions of locally closed sets) the two coincide: a locally closed set with empty interior is nowhere dense, and finite unions of nowhere dense sets are nowhere dense. So there is no actual gap, but Grothendieck does not say this.
Implicitly X and ∅ must belong to F_0 (empty intersections and unions); this is not stated.

ideas.what: Closure on the constructible algebra F is computable purely from the lattice F_0 (closure of A = least element of F_0 containing A)
ideas.modern_name: closure operator induced by a lattice of closed sets; co-Heyting algebra of closed elements

ideas.what: Topology-free reformulation of 'nowhere dense' and of the finite-dimension axiom δ: every chain A_n ⊃ A_{n+1} with A_{n+1} F_0-rare in A_n terminates
ideas.modern_name: descending chain condition on frontiers / dimension axiom of tame (o-minimal-type) geometry; Krull-type dimension of a co-Heyting algebra (iterated co-Heyting boundary)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s) for dim(frontier) < dim; Lawvere (co-Heyting boundary, ~1991) for the algebraic boundary
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 sketches an axiomatic tame topology but, to my knowledge, not these axioms

ideas.what: Criterion for a set family F_0 ⊂ P(X) to be the closed tame sets for some topology: α, β plus existence of a least member of F_0 above each A∖B; the coarsest such topology has closed sets = arbitrary intersections of members of F_0
ideas.modern_name: representation of a co-Heyting (Brouwerian) lattice of sets as the closed sets of a topology; lattice-generated topology (cf. spectral/Stone duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: McKinsey–Tarski 1946 (closed elements form a Brouwerian algebra); Stone duality

missed.claim: Grothendieck's condition γ' is exactly the requirement that F_0 be a co-Heyting (Brouwerian) subalgebra of P(X) whose co-implication is computed as 'least member above the set difference'. His tame-topology axiom δ is then a finite-dimension condition on a co-Heyting algebra, expressible with Lawvere-style boundaries. This links the 'topologie modérée' programme to the algebraic logic of closure algebras and co-Heyting algebras, a connection not drawn in the tame-topology / o-minimal literature as a foundation.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to axiomatise tame topology intrinsically in terms of the lattice F_0 alone, including the dimension axiom δ. The programme of deriving tame-topology results (e.g. the next page's frontier statements) from these lattice axioms is not carried through here.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary general topology and correct. Its interest is historical: a 1974 intrinsic, lattice-theoretic axiomatisation of 'topologie modérée' with a finite-dimension axiom on frontiers. It implicitly rediscovers co-Heyting/McKinsey–Tarski structure. These are notable unpublished details but not deep new results.
